extracted.intended_audience: CFPB staff, bank compliance officers, policymakers, and banking trade associations
extracted.subtask_description: A trade-association comment letter with recommendations for designing and operating the CFPB Advisory Opinion pilot and permanent program, focused on procedural safeguards, scope, publication, and administrative rules to encourage use by banks and other financial service providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Opinions should be limited to specific facts-and-circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for an Advisory Opinion should be grounded in specific facts-and-circumstances and never be based on hypothetical situations or 'what ifs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disallow hypothetical inquiries that would divert Bureau resources; focus on real questions affecting consumers and providers. Because requests come from industry, AOs should reflect specific marketplace needs (examples include serving Limited English Proficiency borrowers, marketing, and other areas where clarification—not regulatory change—is appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Opinions should clearly identify the material facts and circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Each AO should summarize the material facts that define its applicability to the requestor and similarly situated parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide as much information as possible about material facts so the parameters of general applicability are clear. Advisory Opinions should also state whether they are retroactive or only forward-looking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing investigations/enforcement should not categorically bar AOs from unrelated requestors
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that an issue is the subject of an ongoing investigation or enforcement action should not automatically prevent issuance of an AO by or for other, unrelated institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not preclude institutions with no connection to a pending investigation from submitting similar questions; otherwise the Bureau may thwart clarification of issues others legitimately question and discourage submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote public awareness and access to Advisory Opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Opinions should be published and made readily findable and usable by the public and regulated parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish AOs in the Federal Register and on a dedicated Bureau webpage grouped by subject matter; cross-reference AOs on Interactive Bureau Regulations pages; develop an alert system for new AOs; and issue press releases for particularly significant AOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include an option for notice-and-comment on draft Advisory Opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: When an AO would benefit from public feedback, the Bureau should issue a draft AO for public comment before finalizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve efficiency, comments should be limited to the issue at hand and the comment period limited to no more than 30 days; this step can prevent unintended impacts on existing or in-development products and refine the AO for broader usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of a request should not, by itself, lead to examination or investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial institutions must be protected from the prospect that merely submitting an AO request will trigger an examination or investigation on that issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final procedures should include an explicit statement that a request for an AO, standing alone, cannot be the basis for an examination or investigation. If an examination or investigation is appropriate, the Bureau should identify other significant facts and circumstances that justify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redact the name of the requestor from the public Advisory Opinion and protect confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau should redact requester names from the publicly posted AO and treat non-public information as confidential pursuant to its rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow approaches used by other agencies: redact requestor identity in the public version and protect proprietary/confidential submissions under the Bureau's Disclosure of Records and Information rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify required content for Advisory Opinion requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests should include all material facts, a clear articulation of the legal or regulatory question raised, and a proposed interpretation with explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This content requirement mirrors other agencies' approaches and helps staff evaluate and respond to requests effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign administrative responsibility and accountability for the AO program
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau should assign a senior staff member responsibility for the AO program and include clear procedural requirements for staff handling requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should require written confirmation that a request has been received and identify a primary Bureau point-of-contact for the requestor until the AO is signed and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set clear timelines (45 days recommended) with defined extension procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau should adopt a timeline for issuing AOs to encourage use and ensure responsiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend not more than 45 days to issue an AO, with the ability to extend for an additional 45 days accompanied by written communication to the requestor explaining the need for more time. Defined timelines and accountability will promote program use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide written reasons and remediation guidance when declining a request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Bureau declines to issue an AO, it should specify in writing why the request was declined and provide information to help the requestor modify the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering reasons and guidance will reduce uncertainty and help reformulate requests so they become acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a process to delete outdated or obsolete Advisory Opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: The AO program should incorporate a mechanism to remove AOs that are no longer useful or applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use procedures similar to other agencies (e.g., FDIC's process for eliminating outdated policy statements) to reduce regulatory burden and keep the AO corpus current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit third-party submissions on behalf of supervised institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow trade associations, law firms, and other third parties to submit AO requests on behalf of supervised entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting third-party requests assists smaller institutions lacking in-house resources, protects requestor anonymity/competitive concerns, and allows consolidation of common issues from multiple banks into a single submission for broader applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Advisory Opinions as binding interpretive rules under the APA to provide stability and safe-harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: As binding interpretive rules under the Administrative Procedure Act, AOs should bind the agency and can provide banks with safe-harbor protection for good faith reliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binding interpretive status will reduce regulatory uncertainty and 'pendulum swings' with administration changes, allowing banks to allocate resources toward serving consumers and innovating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear issuance and exclusion factors with examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau identified four conditions it will consider for issuance and several factors weighing against issuance; ABA recommends the Bureau incorporate examples to clarify these criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying with examples will help stakeholders understand when AOs are appropriate (e.g., issue not addressable through other channels, noted during examinations, substantive importance, not previously addressed) and when they are not (e.g., subject of planned rulemaking, already addressed by precedent).
